strings.name: Naomi Osaka
strings.role: Tennis player · Four-time major singles champion
strings.summary: Born in Japan and raised and trained in the United States, Osaka reached the top of women’s tennis with a powerful serve and baseline game. Between 2018 and 2021 she won two US Opens and two Australian Opens and became the first Asian singles No.1. Her public discussion of mental health and racial inequality, time away and return after childbirth broadened debate about athletes’ lives.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected career milestones; results and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive results log or live ranking.
strings.influence.rationale: A major champion who has publicly discussed athletes' mental health, exercising social influence across continents.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Four hard-court majors
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Won the US Open in 2018 and 2020 and Australian Open in 2019 and 2021, winning her first four major finals.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: First Asian singles No.1
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Reached the top singles ranking after winning the 2019 Australian Open.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Second-round exit in Tokyo
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Lost 3–6, 5–7 to Mia Pohankova at the Pan Pacific Open.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Back in a US Open semifinal
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Reached finals in Auckland and Montreal and the US Open semifinals, returning to the Top 20.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Returned after childbirth
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Resumed competition after maternity leave, reaching quarterfinals in Doha and ’s-Hertogenbosch.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: French Open withdrawal and mental health
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Withdrew from the French Open and discussed mental-health difficulties, prompting debate about media duties and athlete support.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Fourth major title
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Defeated Jennifer Brady in the Australian Open final for her fourth major singles title.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Second US Open and public advocacy
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Recovered to defeat Victoria Azarenka for a second US Open title while using her platform to highlight racial injustice.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Australian Open and world No.1
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Beat Petra Kvitova to win the Australian Open and became the first Asian singles No.1.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: First Japanese major singles champion
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Defeated Serena Williams in the US Open final to become Japan’s first major singles champion.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: First WTA title at Indian Wells
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Won her first WTA singles title at Indian Wells, launching her breakthrough season.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: WTA main-draw debut
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Qualified in Stanford and beat former US Open champion Samantha Stosur in the first round.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in Osaka
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Born in Osaka to a Haitian father and Japanese mother; moved to the United States at three.
